descriptions.title: Why PowerShell, not Python
descriptions.body: AutoPDF is deliberately Python-free. The server is a single ~7,400-line PowerShell script (AutoPDF-Server.ps1) targeting PS 5.1 syntax so it runs on a vanilla Windows box with nothing installed, and on PS 7+ too. This is what gives AutoPDF its copy-a-folder portability for Windows admins. Constraints follow from PS 5.1: no ternary, no null-coalescing outside PS7, ASCII hyphens only in .ps1 strings (em-dashes corrupt the parser), and Send-Json forces -Depth 10 because the default depth-2 silently truncated nested arrays.

descriptions.title: Bundled engines as separate executables
descriptions.body: Ghostscript, Poppler, Tesseract, Tabula, PDFtk, NAPS2, and a bundled JRE all live under Application/ and are invoked as separate command-line processes (an arm's-length / mere-aggregation relationship). AutoPDF's own code does not link them in-process, which is what keeps AutoPDF's source proprietary even though Ghostscript is AGPL and Poppler/PDFtk/NAPS2 are GPL. The only obligation is on distribution: ship the licenses/ folder and per-engine license files, and do not modify the GPL/AGPL binaries.

descriptions.title: Local-only AI via Ollama
descriptions.body: The single AI path is a local Ollama instance at 127.0.0.1:11434 — there is no OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini integration, by design, because confidential documents are a core use case. /api/ai-chat is page-range aware and parses <thinking> tags from reasoning models into a separate log; /api/template-propose injects the regex library and returns fully configured field payloads plus proposedLibraryAdditions. A specialized variant (autopdf-mapper, built from AutoPDFMapper.Modelfile) understands the three field kinds. AI is opt-in: a Settings toggle greys out every AI surface when Ollama isn't used.

descriptions.title: The template data model — three field kinds
descriptions.technology: The template data model — three field kinds
descriptions.body: Templates are user-defined JSON in Application/templates/. Each field is one of three kinds: zone (a fixed rectangle stored as page fractions), regex_match (a page-text scan with scope all/first/last/N/A-B and strategy first/last/largest/all), or ai_extract (the LLM finds the value at run-time). Invoke-TemplateExtraction runs them in three passes (zones -> regex_match -> ai_extract), each priming the next. A per-field format post-processor normalizes currency/date/number/phone/upper/lower/trim. AI proposes fields but never dictates the schema.

Invoke-TemplateExtraction runs them in three passes, each priming the next. A per-field format post-processor normalizes currency/date/number/phone/upper/lower/trim. descriptions.title: Tagged (anchor-relative) mapping
descriptions.body: Tagged mapping makes a field follow its label across documents instead of being pinned to coordinates. A drawn box becomes the label/anchor (its text is auto-read and the box snaps to it); a value sub-area is positioned relative to that label (right/left/above/below, any size). At run-time Find-AnchorRectFrac + Resolve-TaggedZoneRect re-find the label's text on every document via Poppler word boxes and float the value box to wherever the label appears, falling back to a saved static rectangle if the label isn't found. Get-PdfTextBboxByPage caches word boxes per (path+mtime). It works in both Smart Mapping and the PDF Splitter's Visual Zone Mapper across all four view modes.

Get-PdfTextBboxByPage caches word boxes per (path+mtime). Works in Smart Mapping and the Splitter's Visual Zone Mapper.

descriptions.title: OnBase XML Index DIP output
descriptions.body: The index can be emitted as a Hyland OnBase XML Index Document Import Processor file (Foundation 24.1). Write-IndexXml serializes a config-driven run root with one <NewDocument> per row, an optional <DocTypeName>, one element per metadata column, and a repeatable <FilePath> file reference; ConvertTo-XmlName coerces arbitrary column labels into valid element names. Output is UTF-8 no-BOM, properly XML-escaped, and skips empty keyword elements. It is wired into both emit sites (Index Creator's Invoke-IndexBuild gated on format.alsoXml, and the PDF Splitter gated on indexCsv.xml.enabled) and was verified headless on the 30-file demo set.

descriptions.title: Deployment: launcher, services, tunnel
descriptions.body: AutoPDF.exe is a native C# stub (compiled with Windows' built-in csc.exe) that pings /api/status and either opens the browser or starts the hidden server. Two NSSM services exist under the QI_ naming standard: QI_AutoPDF is a manual, non-started placeholder (the app intentionally runs interactively at logon because Office COM needs a desktop session), and QI_AutoPDFTunnel is an auto-start Cloudflare quick tunnel (tunnel_manager.py) exposing PIN-gated public access at autopdf.quiddityinnovations.com. nssm lives at C:\QIH\engine\bin\nssm.exe. /health and /version stay open for monitoring probes; everything else is PIN-gated.

descriptions.title: OCR roadmap — keeping zero-install
descriptions.body: Tesseract is the live, default OCR engine. A planned second engine adds PP-OCRv5 (later v6) via ONNX Runtime through a .NET binding (RapidOcrNet) — bundled, offline, callable from the existing PowerShell/.NET layer with no Python. The toggle is engine = tesseract|paddle-onnx and device = auto|cpu|cuda, with Tesseract staying the default. The Python/paddlepaddle prototype in PP-OCRv6/ (autopdf_ocr.py) is explicitly rejected for production (~1.5-2.5 GB footprint + AVX crash risk) and is NOT referenced by the server; the ONNX route was chosen specifically to preserve copy-folder portability. Plan approved 2026-06-22, implementation not yet started.
